title: Descent of the geometric Fitting and depth conditions
statement: Let $k$ be a field, $\Omega/k$ an algebraic closure [def-weil-algebraic-closure], $S$ a finitely generated $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], and $\mathfrak p\subset S$ a maximal ideal. Let $\mathfrak q\subset S\otimes_k\Omega$ be a prime whose inverse image in $S$ is $\mathfrak p$. Set $A=S_{\mathfrak p}$, $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak pA$, $F=S/\mathfrak p$, $B=(S\otimes_k\Omega)_{\mathfrak q}$, and $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak qB$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime, def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Put $J=\operatorname{Fit}_1(\Omega_{S/k})$, $J_A=JA$, and $J_B=\operatorname{Fit}_1(\Omega_{(S\otimes_k\Omega)/\Omega})B$, with Kähler differentials [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] and the index-$1$ presentation-minor ideal [lem-trf-fitting-ideal-independence-base-change]. If $J_B=\mathfrak n$ and $\operatorname{depth}B=1$ [def-weil-pbc-depth], then $F/k$ is finite separable [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension], $J_A=\mathfrak m$, and $\operatorname{depth}A=\operatorname{depth}\widehat A=1$, where $\widehat A$ is the $\mathfrak m$-adic completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. In particular the residue map induces $A/J_A\cong F$.

source.place: Tag 0C4D (lemma-nodal), arbitrary-field paragraphs descending the geometric first-Fitting field stalk and depth one; differential base change as in Algebra Tags 00RV and 00RT.

proof.text: Choose algebra generators $s_1,\ldots,s_d$ of $S/k$. By the additive and Leibniz relations of [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials], the differential of a polynomial in these generators is an $S$-linear combination of $\mathrm ds_i$ (induct on sums and products, with constants having differential zero). The symbol construction in that node says all differentials generate the module. Thus $\Omega_{S/k}$ is a finite $S$-module, including when $d=0$.

Put $C=S\otimes_k\Omega$. By [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-base-change], $\Omega_{C/\Omega}\cong C\otimes_S\Omega_{S/k}$. Apply clause (2) of [lem-trf-fitting-ideal-independence-base-change] first to $S\to C$ and then to $C\to B$: the index-$1$ ideals satisfy $\operatorname{Fit}_1(\Omega_{C/\Omega})=JC$ and $(JC)B=J_B=\mathfrak n$. For $j\in J$, its image in $B$ lies in $\mathfrak qB$, so its image in $C$ lies in $\mathfrak q$; contraction under localization at a prime gives this directly from the fraction criterion. Since $\mathfrak q\cap S=\mathfrak p$, we have $J\subseteq\mathfrak p$.

source.place: Tag 0C4D (lemma-nodal), arbitrary-field paragraph defining Z; Algebra Tag 00RV and More on Algebra Tag 07ZA (lemma-fitting-ideal-basics), part (3).

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-geometric-field-stalk-descent] to $S$, $\mathfrak p$ and the given prime $\mathfrak q$. Its unconditional clauses give finiteness of $F/k$, maximality of $\mathfrak q$, and the structural $\Omega$-algebra identification $C/\mathfrak q=\kappa(\mathfrak q)\cong\Omega$. Since $J_B=\mathfrak n$, the same residue map identifies $B/J_B$ with $\Omega$ as an $\Omega$-algebra.

source.place: Tag 0C4D (lemma-nodal), the geometric first-Fitting field stalk; Algebra Tag 00FV (theorem-nullstellensatz).

proof.text: Set $T=S/J$ and $\mathfrak p_T=\mathfrak p/J$; these are a finite type $k$-algebra and a maximal ideal, with $T/\mathfrak p_T=F$. Tensor $J\to S\to T\to0$ over $k$ with $\Omega$. By [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-right-exact], the map $C\to T\otimes_k\Omega$, $s\otimes a\mapsto\bar s\otimes a$, is surjective with kernel the image of $J\otimes_k\Omega$. That image is exactly $JC$: its pure tensors are $(j\otimes1)(1\otimes a)$, and multiplication of such a tensor by $s\otimes b$ gives $sj\otimes ab$ with $sj\in J$. Hence $T\otimes_k\Omega\cong C/JC$ as $\Omega$-algebras. The prime $\mathfrak r=\mathfrak q/JC$ of this quotient contracts to $\mathfrak p_T$.

source.place: Tag 0C4D (lemma-nodal), pass to the closed subscheme Z defined by J; Algebra Tag 00DF (lemma-tensor-product-exact).

proof.text: The fraction maps $(c+JC)/(v+JC)\mapsto(c/v)+J_B$, with $v\notin\mathfrak q$, identify $(C/JC)_{\mathfrak q/JC}$ with $B/J_B$. The inverse sends the class of $c/v$ to the displayed quotient fraction. They are well defined: the fraction equality relation in either quotient says that some element outside $\mathfrak q$ annihilates the difference modulo $JC$, and clearing denominators gives precisely membership in $(JC)B=J_B$. The maps preserve multiplication and are inverse on every fraction. Thus $(T\otimes_k\Omega)_{\mathfrak r}\cong\Omega$ as $\Omega$-algebras by step 3. Apply the conditional clause of [lem-trf-geometric-field-stalk-descent], now to $T$ and $\mathfrak p_T$. It gives $T_{\mathfrak p_T}\cong F$ via the residue map and $F/k$ finite separable.

source.place: Tag 0C4D (lemma-nodal), arbitrary-field paragraph: the geometric field stalk of Z descends to a separable field stalk.

proof.text: The same quotient-fraction formulas, with $S,J,\mathfrak p$ in place of $C,JC,\mathfrak q$, give $A/J_A\cong T_{\mathfrak p_T}$. The resulting map $A/J_A\to F$ sends the class of $s/u$ to $\bar s/\bar u$, so it is the residue map and is an isomorphism by step 5. Its kernel before quotienting is both $J_A$ and $\mathfrak m$, giving $J_A=\mathfrak m$ and the required residue isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0C4D (lemma-nodal), descent of the first Fitting ideal to the maximal ideal.

proof.text: The quotient $C\to C/\mathfrak q\cong\Omega$ of step 3 restricts to a $k$-embedding $\iota:F\hookrightarrow\Omega$, because its restriction to $S$ has kernel $\mathfrak p$. On pure tensors it is $s\otimes a\mapsto\iota(\bar s)a$, so $\mathfrak q$ is exactly the kernel of this evaluation map. Apply [lem-trf-separable-evaluation-local-base-change] with $K=\Omega$ and the finite separable extension from step 5. It states that $A,B$ are Noetherian local rings, $A\to B$ is a faithfully flat local homomorphism, and $B/\mathfrak mB\cong\Omega$ (also $\mathfrak mB=\mathfrak n$). All these assertions concern the original given prime $\mathfrak q$.

source.place: Tags 0C4Y (lemma-change-fields-flat) and 0C50 (lemma-change-fields-algebraic-unramified), finite separable closed-fibre case.

proof.text: A nonzero field has depth zero by [def-weil-pbc-depth, def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]: its maximal ideal is zero, the empty regular sequence exists, and any positive-length sequence in that ideal starts with zero, whose multiplication on the nonzero field is not injective. Thus the closed fibre $B/\mathfrak mB\cong\Omega$ of step 7 has depth zero. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-depth-formula] to its flat local map $A\to B$ between Noetherian local rings. It gives $1=\operatorname{depth}B=\operatorname{depth}A+0$, hence $\operatorname{depth}A=1$.

For the Noetherian local ring $A$ of step 7, [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-local-ring] gives that $\widehat A$ is local, with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m\widehat A$ and residue field $\widehat A/\mathfrak m\widehat A\cong A/\mathfrak m=F$. In particular the canonical map $A\to\widehat A$ is local. By [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian], $\widehat A$ is Noetherian, and [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-completion-flat] says this canonical map is flat. Its closed fibre is the nonzero field $F$, of depth zero by the regular-sequence argument of step 8. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-depth-formula] gives $\operatorname{depth}\widehat A=\operatorname{depth}A+0=1$, completing every clause.
